title: Go SDK: schema-driven unmarshallers and streaming combinators
creator: Marcus Patel
description: Goal: provide a set of Go SDK utilities that make decoding both batch and streaming LLM responses ergonomically typed, resilient to partial/fragmented events, and compatible with generic application models. Deliver a small surface of well-documented primitives: a schema-driven UnmarshalInto[T], composable StreamCombinators for handling partial JSON fragments, and a RetryableStream wrapper that applies backpressure-aware retry logic and preserves parsed state across retries. These utilities should be safe for production usage, test-covered, and have clear examples for common patterns (structured output, tool-calling, chat messages).
acceptance_criteria: UnmarshalInto[T] implemented as a small, well-documented generic helper that returns typed models and clear errors for validation failures
Stream combinators implemented: FrameSplitter, JsonReassembler, FieldCombinator (to merge partial tokens for nested structs)
RetryableStream wrapper with configurable backoff and a hook to rehydrate decoder state when retrying mid-stream
End-to-end examples added: structured JSON response decoding, tool-call extraction, and streaming chat messages with attachments
Unit tests cover fragmented input, invalid token sequences, and retry edge cases; include a small property-based test for random chunk boundaries
Performance benchmark shows <10% CPU overhead versus raw json.Decoder on typical 8k avg token responses and no regression in latency p50/p95 for streaming endpoints
Docs page with migration notes and 3 copy-paste examples in examples/ directory
Security review completed (if streaming retries rehydrate sensitive buffers, ensure no secret retention)
progress_updates: 2026-03-03: Spike finished — validated approach using io.Pipe + bufio.Reader to handle arbitrary chunk boundaries. Found two failure modes: nested arrays split across chunks and escaped characters across boundaries.
2026-03-06: Implemented initial FrameSplitter and JsonReassembler prototypes. Baseline tests for fragmented arrays pass. POC in internal playground: examples/stream-reassemble.md
2026-03-09: Added generic UnmarshalInto[T] with optional validator hook. Chose to use encoding/json + small validation layer rather than a full schema library to keep binary size low.

2026-03-11: Built RetryableStream prototype that records decoder checkpoints (field offsets) to allow resume after a transient 502. Decided against full state machine capture to avoid coupling to downstream decoder internals.
2026-03-13: Benchmarks run — overhead ~6% vs raw json.Decoder on our microbench harness. Need a follow-up to optimize the reassembler buffer growth pattern.
comments: PM Priya: Please include a short migration guide for existing users who use json.Decoder directly.
Design Leo: For typed models, let's prefer explicit model tags (json schema via struct tags) instead of reflection-heavy runtime checks. Keep the surface small.
SRE Dana: When RetryableStream retries mid-stream, ensure we emit monotonic event ids so console traceability remains correct.
Reviewer Jonas: API naming suggestion: UnmarshalInto[T] -> UnmarshalTo[T] or DecodeAs[T]? Ava: leaning UnmarshalInto[T] because it reads like encoding/json. Open to bikeshed in PR.
